Plan for Phase 68 at 20d14ac: docs/phases/cockpit-turn-bar-and-watcher-drawer.md. The roadmap's old Phase 68 is split: this phase is the header (turn bar + watcher drawer); the lanes became Phase 68b (depends on 68). Grounded in a live look at the cockpit on 2026-09-20 and a line-referenced map of cockpit.js/html/css and their tests.

The problem: the header is up to seven equal pills (renderNow, cockpit.js:149); 'watcher: on' has nothing behind it; cockpit.js reads neither now.watcher.beat / last_event nor /api/watcher/events (Phase 67).

The plan:
1. cockpit_api.headline(now) — a pure function over what now_payload() already assembles — returns {state, tone, text, age_s, role, agent}; first-match table of 11 states written out in the doc (needs-you, turn-lost, working, launching, paused, watcher-off, stalled [beat.state == stale with a turn owed], starting, waiting-terminal, approved/aborted, idle). The browser only appends the ticking age. watcher.beat gains 'text' (watchlog.describe_beat), and 'tagteam watch status' prints the headline as its first line, so every surface words it the same way.
2. Turn bar: one dominant <button aria-expanded> replaces chip-owed / chip-inflight / chip-paused / chip-watcher; chip-cycle, chip-gate, chip-notes, Pause stay as secondary items. Needs-you cards unchanged (action surface vs status surface).
3. Watcher drawer under the header (not a modal, not a tab): facts (pid/mode/started, last look, paused, Start/Stop moved here), WHY the cockpit cannot run turns (START.headless.errors — today the notify-mode confirm gives no reason; or 'agents are in their terminals' for a tab watcher), and the event history from /api/watcher/events — info lines hidden by default, refreshed on the existing tick only while open, createElement/textContent only.
4. Tests: a Python table test for every row and the priority order; the new JS in its own banner-delimited slice run under node with the existing _DOM_STUB technique; string guards changed deliberately (chip-owed/inflight/watcher move from the required-id list to the must-stay-absent list; turn-bar and watcher-drawer join the required list) and each change listed in the submission.
5. Criterion 7 is 'seen, not assumed': Playwright screenshots of a real headless run, the drawer with real history, watcher-off, this repo under its iTerm2 watcher, and a stalled state produced by SIGSTOP-ing a scratch watcher rather than by faking the payload.

Please look hardest at: the state table's priority order (is 'paused' correctly below 'working'/'launching'? should a stale beat ever outrank 'watcher-off'?); deriving the sentence server-side vs in JS; and removing four pills whose ids existing guards pin.

Verified while planning: roadmap check ok (77 phases, 33 edges); gate check --skip-tests plan-doc ok; now_payload's keys checked against the table's inputs (the resend window is not in the payload, so waiting-terminal uses the 15-minute threshold chip-owed already uses). Nothing implemented.

Reviewed plan at 20d14ac against now_payload, watchlog.status_lines, and the gate/panel/headless marker writers. The header/drawer split, server-side pure derivation, deliberate guard updates and real-browser verification are appropriate. Working before paused is correct because pausing holds future dispatch rather than stopping an active turn. Watcher-off should precede stale heartbeat: an old beat is not evidence of a currently stalled process.

Three plan corrections before implementation:

1. Correct the turn-lost predicate. now_payload sets inflight.pid_alive to False for pid=None, not just a dead child. Gate markers deliberately carry pid=None throughout the gate (gatekeeper.py around line 702); cycle/panel markers also begin without a child pid. As written, row 2 wins over 'Pre-check running' and over legitimate startup. Specify kind/owner-aware liveness, distinguishing no child yet (or no child by design) from a confirmed exited process. Keep existing keys compatible, adding derived facts if necessary. Tests must use real marker shapes: live gate owner + pid=None, cycle/panel startup before spawn, live child, confirmed dead child, and dead owner. Do not blindly promote the existing chip's pid_alive predicate into the dominant sentence.

2. Make the owed-turn table exhaustive and honest. Headless + owed + running with beat.state none/previous (older watcher, missing/unwritable beat, identity mismatch) currently matches neither starting (requires fresh) nor waiting-terminal and can fall through to 'Nothing in progress'. Unknown watcher mode from process scanning has the same hole. Add a neutral waiting/status-unknown fallback that keeps the owed agent visible without claiming a launch or a terminal. Notify mode is also only a notification: it cannot establish that the agent is 'in its terminal'. Give it appropriate wording. Cover each missing-beat/unknown-mode case in the table tests. An actually working terminal state should not be presented as a confirmed dead/stalled agent merely because the watcher has stopped; keep the distinction between dispatch machinery and agent execution explicit.

3. Specify a genuinely read-only CLI input path. watchlog.status_lines currently reads only inflight, watcher, beat, history and pause; it does not already assemble the headline's state/cycle/launch/last-turn inputs. Simply calling now_payload from watch status would invoke db.connect, which creates/migrates the database in ordinary mode (the TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY guard prevents that only when set). Plan either shared side-effect-free fact collection or a minimal read-only input builder using the same headline function. Test watch status without TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY as well as with it on a DB-less project, asserting no database/runtime files are created or modified.

Presentation detail: the stalled example embeds '6m ago' even though text is specified as age-free and the browser appends age_s; choose one ticking age representation to avoid duplicate/frozen ages. The drawer should preserve a user's scroll position when they scroll back, following new rows only while already at the bottom.

No implementation exists yet; no tests were run for this plan review. No interjections present.
